function: Captain Michael's working core: a covered shop where salvage becomes machines, and where the crew's housing, training and command capacity is measured. Brief section 5.6 -- Michael's buildings make machines, capacity and services, and they never make people.
height_class: [needs decision: height class for building.machine_shop -- brief section 20, exact standard building dimensions]

tier_states.notes: A roof, a bench and a door. Enough to repair what the wreck gave up.
Powered tooling. The first tier that builds a machine rather than mending one. The requirement flag is an Open placeholder; S13 owns what satisfies it.
The core proper: command space and integration capacity alongside the shop floor.

dungeon_relationship: Provisional: a ruined machine shop is a small, shallow site of benches and dead tooling. S9 owns the generation signature; nothing here is a grammar.
loot_relationship: Provisional: parts and tools rather than treasure. S10 owns loot tables; this string is prose no code reads.

notes: Brief section 5.6 and section 20: this record lists concept key michael, so a human_role production rule is refused outright -- by BuildingDefinition::validate and by the buildings block in tools/src/validate.mjs. The three rules here make a machine, capacity and a service. recruitment_support is deliberately empty: Michael's faction grows by recruitment, migration, relationships, rescue and factional change, never because a building said so.

Open (brief section 20, exact resource list): construction_cost and every production output_key carry the single placeholder resource.open.needs_decision at amount-bearing but meaningless weight 0 for cost. No resource category is invented here, exactly as C9 did for resource_priorities.

Open (brief section 20, exact standard building dimensions): height_class is a needs-decision placeholder, maximum_slope is 0 because the world graph carries no slope, and footprint_cells / clearance_cells are shares of CELL_CAPACITY_CELLS rather than metres. B11 and O3 own real geometry.

Open (brief section 20, capture versus destruction rules by building type): capture_rules and ruin_state are chosen here, per record, as S3 required -- a shop is worth taking, and a burnt shop still occupies its floor. The choice is this record's, not the engine's.
Open: construction_requirements flags are requirement.open.needs_decision.* placeholders. S13 decides what a faction must hold to unlock a tier; nothing reads these strings today.
Open: allowed_terrain is empty because the authored terrain key space does not exist yet; empty means the placement rules alone decide.
Provisional: dungeon_relationship and loot_relationship are prose. S9 and S10 own those systems.
